subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep bootstrap-extra-files limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: The change affects deterministic startup context and the public file-loading contract for hook configuration, so it needs maintainer product/security intent before implementation lands.

options.title: Approve repaired hook contract
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path once the implementation preserves path guards, budgets, session filtering, and documentation.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and keep users on current AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, and recognized bootstrap-file composition patterns.

options.title: Defer to a broader context API
options.body: Keep this issue open only as design input for a future context-file API or workspace capability convention rather than changing the hook now.

recommendation.title: Approve repaired hook contract
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path once the implementation preserves path guards, budgets, session filtering, and documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the original hook and loader contract that the product-direction decision would change.
